transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. To start, can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, yeah. Um… what finally scared me into making the appointment is that I keep making these really dumb technical mistakes at work that I absolutely know better than to make. I’m a camera operator and editor, so details matter, and I’ll do things like label camera cards wrong, or miss a timecode note, or export a client cut with the wrong lower-third on it.

And the worst part is, it’s not like I don’t know the workflow. I do. I’ve done this for years. I’ll even think I’ve checked something, sometimes more than once, and then it still goes out wrong. It’s embarrassing, and it’s starting to make me really nervous because these are the kinds of mistakes that can cost time, trust, and money. I keep thinking, “How did I miss that?” and I don’t have a good answer, so… yeah, that’s why I’m here.
How has your sleep been lately—are you having trouble falling asleep, staying asleep, or waking up feeling unrested?

Um… I don’t know that I have a clean answer for that. I haven’t really been tracking it closely, honestly. Some nights feel fine and other nights I’m just kind of… up later than I meant to be, but I’m not sure if that’s “trouble falling asleep” in the way you mean or just me not getting myself to bed.

I don’t think I’ve noticed a clear pattern of waking up a lot or anything like that. And waking up unrested… I mean, sometimes, but I feel like everyone says that, so I don’t know how much weight to put on it. I guess I’d say sleep hasn’t been the thing that made me come in, but I also probably haven’t paid enough attention to give you a precise answer.
Thinking back, would you say you've struggled with this kind of distractibility and forgetfulness since childhood or your school years, or is this more of a new change that's shown up recently?

Yeah, no, it’s definitely not brand-new. I mean, the work mistakes are what finally made it feel urgent, because there are real consequences now, but when I think back, there were signs pretty early.

Like in elementary school, I remember teachers moving my desk around a lot—not because I was being malicious or anything, but because I was always out of my seat, or I’d blurt out answers before they finished the question, or I’d end up bothering the kid next to me before I even realized I was doing it. It was like my body or my mouth would go first and my brain would catch up afterward.

I didn’t think of it as “distractibility” back then, obviously. I just thought I was in trouble a lot, or that I was too much. But looking back, yeah, it was there during school years, not just something that suddenly appeared recently.
Aside from work, do you find yourself worrying excessively about several different things in your day-to-day life—things you have a hard time controlling or turning off?

I’m not totally sure how to answer that, because I do worry about things, but I don’t know if I’d call it “excessive” in that broad, constant way.

Like, I can definitely get stuck worrying when I’ve made a mistake or think I might have missed something, and then I’ll replay it in my head and feel keyed up about it. But if you mean am I worrying all day about lots of different areas—money, health, family, the future, random bad things happening—I don’t know that I’ve noticed that as the main pattern.

It’s more like I’m stressed about specific things when they’re in front of me, especially if there’s a consequence. I’m not walking around feeling like I can’t turn off worry about everything, at least not in a way I’ve really identified. I guess I’d say… not really, or not that I’m aware of.
Over the past couple of weeks, have you noticed a persistent low mood or a loss of interest or pleasure in activities you'd normally enjoy?

I don’t think so? Not in a persistent way, anyway. I mean, I’ve had days where I feel frustrated or kind of worn down, especially if I’m already annoyed with myself about not getting things done the way I meant to, but I wouldn’t say I’ve been sitting in a low mood for two weeks straight.

And with interest or enjoyment… I haven’t really noticed losing interest in things across the board. Like, I still want to do things I normally like, at least in theory. Sometimes I don’t get around to them or I’m too mentally scattered to settle into them, but that feels different from not caring about them or not enjoying them.

So I guess my answer is no, not really. I haven’t noticed a clear ongoing depression-type feeling or a loss of pleasure lately.
